subject.title: feat(channels): core-owned durable ingress drain — one turn-adoption lifecycle, Telegram first

question: Should OpenClaw permanently publish the core ingress-drain and turn-adoption seam to plugins, with compatibility for the shipped reply lifecycle API?
rationale: The architecture is technically strong, but choosing a permanent plugin SDK contract and its deprecation window is a product/API ownership decision that automated review cannot make.

options.title: Land with compatibility bridge
options.body: Approve the narrow seam, preserve shipped lifecycle members as deprecated adapters, then rebase and rerun exact-head proof.

options.title: Keep the seam core-internal
options.body: Migrate bundled Telegram through an internal core contract and defer public SDK exposure until another external channel consumer proves the API.

recommendation.title: Land with compatibility bridge
recommendation.body: Approve the narrow seam, preserve shipped lifecycle members as deprecated adapters, then rebase and rerun exact-head proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work owns the plugin SDK surface-reduction and shared channel-runtime direction most directly.
